newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl tells employers to "roll up sleeves" for jobs.
newsitem.headline: Kohl tells employers to "roll up sleeves" for jobs.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl urged employers on Saturday to "roll up their sleeves" and create jobs to ensure Germany's prosperity at the heart of a European currency union.

Kohl told a party congress of his Christian Social Union (CSU) coalition partners the government had made its contribution to the jobs market by cutting labour costs and it was now up to employers to play their part.
"I expect the employers to roll up their sleeves and say "Now we're going to create jobs'," the chancellor said.
He told the congress the German economy also needed a new wave of small and medium-sized businesses.
"We have to do more so people form their own businesses," he said, calling on banks and other financial institutions to make more risk capital available for prospective entrepreneurs.
Kohl also reaffirmed his commitment to Europe's planned single currency and to the criteria laid down in the Maastrcht Treaty for prospective member countries.
"The criteria must be applied -- and not just a little," the chancellor said in his speech to the CSU, the arch-conservative sister party of his own Christian Democratic Union (CDU).

The CSU, led by Finance Minister Theo Waigel, also passed a resolution on European policy calling for more concrete measures to ensure the stability of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), due to begin in 1999.
Waigel is a leading advocate of a strict "stability pact" among members of EMU, with tough sanctions for states which do not stick to strict budget targets.
